_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); oilfield services signals

pit_profile.why: Baker Hughes: 'Baker Hughes Incorporated is a Delaware corporation engaged in the oilfield services industry'; 'Within our oilfield operations, the primary driver of our businesses is our customers’ capital and operating expenditures dedicated to oil and natural gas exploration, field development and production'; 'Our revenue is predominately generated from the sale of products and services to major, national, and independent oil and natural gas companies worldwide, and is dependent on spending by our customers for oil and natural gas exploration, field development and production'; 'We operate in a highly competitive environment, which may adversely affect our ability to succeed'; 'In addition, demand for oil and natural gas could be impacted by environmental regulation, including cap and trade legislation, regulation of hydraulic fracturing, carbon taxes and the cost for carbon capture and sequestration related regulations' (its own FY2015 10-K): revenues and earnings that follow customers' drilling and production spending through the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, which an oilfield services company does not hold, so the greenhouse-gas wording stays here

classification.quality_note: Baker Hughes: 'Baker Hughes Incorporated is a Delaware corporation engaged in the oilfield services industry'; 'Within our oilfield operations, the primary driver of our businesses is our customers’ capital and operating expenditures dedicated to oil and natural gas exploration, field development and production'; 'Our revenue is predominately generated from the sale of products and services to major, national, and independent oil and natural gas companies worldwide, and is dependent on spending by our customers for oil and natural gas exploration, field development and production'; 'We operate in a highly competitive environment, which may adversely affect our ability to succeed'; 'In addition, demand for oil and natural gas could be impacted by environmental regulation, including cap and trade legislation, regulation of hydraulic fracturing, carbon taxes and the cost for carbon capture and sequestration related regulations' (its own FY2015 10-K): revenues and earnings that follow customers' drilling and production spending through the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, which an oilfield services company does not hold, so the greenhouse-gas wording stays here. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 1.16x; -8% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.83; conservative 2yr +48%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -74.3%/yr (worst year FY06-FY14, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +-51.8%/yr (Q4 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr ex-FY15 median

BULL.desc: EPS +0.4%/yr (FY06-FY14 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +74.5%/yr (best 2-yr run FY06-FY14); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: BHI (retrospective, 2016-04-22) ◐ WATCHLIST — Ratio B 1.16x (91.4% downside to Bear $4 / +78.8% upside to Bull $83) | Adj composite 1.50 vs market 2.33: gap -0.83 [OVERVALUED] | -8% above the EPP floor $51 (12x FY16E $4.22) | Conservative 2-yr case: +48.4% total (+24.2%/yr) | At 11.0x FY16E the 15% hurdle price $61 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; North America revenue -65.6% and revenue outside North America -33.3% in Q4 2015, forward revenues -48.8% (no Q1 2016 revenue guide, Q4 2015 revenue as reported); ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining; no theme in scope has dated evidence.
